name: June of 44
label: Quarterstick
lede: Jeff Mueller, Sean Meadows, Fred Erskine and Doug Scharin came from four cities and four bands, cut a record in Brooklyn in four days, then spent five years stretching the template into dub, strings and a fifteen-minute closer.

eras.title: Four bands, one name
eras.text: Rodan and Codeine are done, and the four of them live nowhere near each other. They book a studio anyway.

years.cap: June of 44 on a Brooklyn rooftop
years.src: POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller · Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years · Wikipedia: June of 44
years.h: Rodan's guitarist recruits three people from three other bands
years.p: Jeff Mueller brings Rodan's angles, Fred Erskine brings [[Hoover|d691df14-6955-4cae-9dcc-318fb7d75984]]'s bass and trumpet, Doug Scharin drums from Rex, and Sean Meadows (also of [[Lungfish|5af88bca-9c13-424a-b63c-b5c96c69cb0e]]) a second guitar.
years.xp:
The four had met on tour in 1992 and 1993 and came together in November 1994. Mueller bounced between Chicago, Louisville and New York, Meadows was in Baltimore, Scharin in Williamsburg, Erskine in Washington, D.C. Mueller recalls it moving so fast that nobody could tell if the music was any good.

He has described the plan as a few weeks to make a record, then everyone sailing off in other directions. It turned into five years.

years.src: Wikipedia: June of 44 · POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller
years.h: Named for a stack of letters between Henry Miller and Anaïs Nin
years.p: The band took its name from the correspondence between the two writers.
years.xp: The nautical theme that runs through the first three records was Mueller's own project rather than a group decision, he says. He also stamped it on the objects: he printed the first record's packaging on his own letterpress, his first printing job.

years.src: Wikipedia: Engine Takes to the Water · Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years · POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller · AllMusic: June of 44 Biography
yt: Live at The Middle East, Cambridge, December 1995
years.h: Engine Takes to the Water goes down in four days in Brooklyn
years.p: Eight songs recorded in mid-December 1994 at Plantain Recording House, with [[James Murphy|6b70c46c-5c83-4cc7-99c1-e76b68919c6a]] behind the board. Quarterstick QS32.
years.xp: Murphy went on to found [[LCD Soundsystem|2aaf7396-6ab8-40f3-9776-a41c42c8e26b]]. The record came out on CD, cassette and LP on Quarterstick, the label that had put out Rodan's Rusty the year before. AllMusic hears Rodan's angular riffs, extreme dynamics and shifting meters, with more room around them.

eras.title: Longer songs, a second band
eras.text: Bob Weston takes over the board and the songs stretch out. Mueller starts Shipping News before June of 44 has made its third record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tropics and Meridians · POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller · Wikipedia: Rodan (band)
years.h: Tropics and Meridians opens with nine minutes of "Anisette"
years.p: Six songs, 36 minutes, recorded in Chicago with [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]] producing. Quarterstick QS44.
years.xp:
Weston had produced Rodan's Rusty and stayed for the next two records. Every song is credited to all four members.

"Anisette" alone takes up nearly a quarter of the album.

years.h: Mueller and Jason Noble start Shipping News on the side
years.p: Mueller and his Rodan bandmate [[Jason Noble|1a30edd1-b7ee-4d9f-ae1c-af8cd4759718]] form [[Shipping News|d6ed84da-0414-4c44-ace7-ae491ce7d999]] with drummer Kyle Crabtree. Their debut Save Everything came out on Quarterstick in 1997.
years.xp: Shipping News would outlast June of 44, with four albums on Quarterstick between 1997 and 2005. Noble was diagnosed with synovial sarcoma in 2009 and died on August 4, 2012, at 40, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller
years.h: The Anatomy of Sharks keeps the ocean theme going
years.p: An EP that slots in between Tropics and Meridians and Four Great Points.
years.xp: The sea imagery runs through the first three albums and the band's titles. Mueller says it was mostly his idea, not a group decision.

eras.title: Dub, strings and a fifteen-minute closer
eras.text: Violin, electronics, organ and a tube radio join the guitars. The last record leaves more ideas than time.

years.cap: Poster for Fugazi, June of 44 and Elliott at Highland Hall, Louisville, Nov 27, 1998
q: Each subsequent record was increasingly more collaborative.
years.src: Wikipedia: Four Great Points · Leo Weekly: A conversation with Jeff Mueller of June of 44
years.h: A year and two studios for Four Great Points
years.p: Recorded between August 1996 and August 1997 at Electrical Audio in Chicago and Sound Techniques in Boston, with Weston producing.
years.xp:
Julie Liu adds violin, Bundy K. Brown of [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]] adds electronics, and Erskine plays trumpet. Pitchfork gave it a 9.0, and the Chicago Reader called it a hypnotic blend of rock, dub, ambient and orchestral pop.

Mueller says each record after the first got more collaborative, which is why the instrumentation gets more mixed up.

years.h: The four-piece play "Sharks and Sailors" live
years.p: Footage of the band playing "Sharks and Sailors" live in 1998, the year of Four Great Points.

years.src: Discogs: June Of 44 - In The Fishtank
years.h: Two days in a Dutch studio with an old organ and a tube radio
years.p: Konkurrent's In the Fishtank series gives June of 44 its sixth slot, recorded during their European tour.
years.xp: The liner notes call it the missing link between Four Great Points and Anahata. The six tracks include "Henry's Revenge" and "Every Free Day a Good Day". Konkurrent was the Dutch label behind the series.

years.src: Wikipedia: Anahata (album) · Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years · Wikipedia: June of 44
years.h: Anahata ends on "Peel Away Velleity", fifteen minutes long
years.p: Eight songs, about 50 minutes, recorded in January 1999 at Electrical Audio, with Weston again.
years.xp:
Reviews split. Exclaim! called it the band's most satisfying outing to date, CMJ found the unison shouting a drag, and Pitchfork gave it 7.8. Sources disagree on the label, and Wikipedia's band page lists it as Konkurrent.

Mueller later told Rolling Stone the sessions were "pretty tough" and that many of the songs felt underdeveloped.

years.src: Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years · Leo Weekly: A conversation with Jeff Mueller of June of 44 · Wikipedia: June of 44 · Wikipedia: Jeff Mueller · Wikipedia: Hoover (band)
years.h: The first run ends with one last show in November 1999
years.p: The four scatter into side projects: Mueller to Shipping News, Erskine to Abilene, Scharin to HiM, Meadows to Everlasting the Way, later Letter E.
years.xp: Mueller says the side projects did not cause the split, only that the band ended. He released a solo album, Fold and Perish, that year on Monitor. Scharin's HiM had started in 1995, and Erskine had played in the Crownhate Ruin alongside Hoover.

eras.title: A birthday party in Sicily
eras.text: One phone call from Catania ends a nineteen-year break, and the new record turns out to be an old one.

years.big: "We just felt like it had to happen."
years.src: Stereogum: June Of 44 Reunite For First Shows In 19 Years · Leo Weekly: A conversation with Jeff Mueller of June of 44 · Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years
years.h: Uzeda calls, and June of 44 plays for the first time in 19 years
years.p: Mueller on saying yes when the Sicilian band [[Uzeda|9cb56cf1-bd4a-4d59-8ecb-dc412f595dd3]] asked them to play its 30th anniversary in Catania. Catania May 25 and 26, then Turin, Bologna and Rome.
years.xp:
As Stereogum listed it, the Italian run was Catania on May 25 and 26, Turin on May 28, Bologna on May 29 and Rome on May 30. Mueller says that when Uzeda's Agostino called, it just felt like it had to happen.

The band kept playing through 2018 and 2019, including Bay Area dates in fall 2019, before the recording sessions for the next record.

years.cap: Jeff Mueller, Sean Meadows, Fred Erskine and Doug Scharin
years.src: Rolling Stone: How June of 44 Found Closure on Their First Album in 21 Years · POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller · Wikipedia: June of 44
years.h: Revisionist gives the old songs a second try
years.p: Revisionist: Adaptations & Future Histories in the Time of Love and Survival re-records and remixes older material. Announced in July, out in August on Broken Clover.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone reported the album was recorded in a California studio in 2019. Mueller said of the Anahata sessions: "The session for Anahata was pretty tough; many of the songs felt underdeveloped." The new project was a chance to think through material the band had never given itself time to consider.

He also said he wanted to present the songs as they were written, not necessarily as they were played in the 1990s.

eras.title: Tokyo, then two guitars
eras.text: The reunion goes to Japan and Australia and gets a live record, while Mueller and Meadows start a duo.

years.src: POST-TRASH: An All-En-Compass-Ing Conversation With June of 44's Jeff Mueller · Wikipedia: June of 44
years.h: Japan and Australia sell out, and Tokyo gets taped
years.p: The band toured Japan and Australia in 2023. The March 9 show at Club Fever in Tokyo was recorded.
years.xp: Mueller describes the recent shows as more ceremony and celebration than youthful aggression, and says the reunion was about understanding the material more than replicating the 1990s.

years.h: Mueller and Meadows debut as Flowting Clowds
years.p: The duo put out a first single in November 2025 and play shows across the northern U.S.

years.h: Live in Tokyo arrives, taped at Club Fever in 2023
years.p: A live album recorded March 9, 2023 at Club Fever, announced on Bandcamp in January 2026.
